items.title: Lizzie Miles Interview, 1951-01-18
items.q: Then I Made On The Columbia with Clarence Williams.

ctx.x: They're the writers of the piece. Clarence Williams is, I mean, Spencer Williams is the writer of the Haitian blues. See? But Russell Robinson is the one who played the piano. And you played the gazook. And I played the gazook. That's right.

items.title: Lizzie Miles Interview, 1951-01-18
items.q: I made the Haitian blues. Haitian blues, I think, and Black Man Be On Your Way. On the Brunswick.

ctx.x: You know, I looked through here and I didn't find any list in here of Russell Robinson on Brunswick with you. You say you made a record with him?
That's right. I made the Haitian blues. Haitian blues, I think, and Black Man Be On Your Way. On the Brunswick.
They got that as Clarence Johnson and Spencer Williams.
